summary: HETA proposes a three-component token attribution method for decoder-only LLMs (target-conditioned attention-value rollout gating, HVP-based Hessian sensitivity, and KL-under-masking), evaluated on three benchmarks plus a new curated dataset with a new DSA metric. The problem is relevant, the baseline suite is broad, and the ablation/robustness plan is appropriate in design. However, the paper has serious internal inconsistencies (DSA values in Table 1 exceed the metric's own definitional range; the DSA definition as written is circular), an unaddressed evaluation confound (a KL-masking-based method scored primarily on masking/perturbation-based faithfulness metrics), implausibly large effect sizes without significance testing, and mischaracterization of LLM-generated labels as 'human annotations'. These are substantive evidentiary problems, not cosmetic ones.
strengths: Well-motivated problem: faithful token-level attribution for autoregressive decoder-only models is under-served, and the critique of attention-based and first-order methods is accurate and well-cited.

Broad empirical design in principle: 9 baselines including recent generative-attribution methods (ContextCite, TDD, PML, ReAgent, SEA-CoT), 4 models spanning 3B-70B, 3 established benchmarks plus a curated probe dataset, plus decoding-hyperparameter sensitivity and syntactic-rephrasing robustness studies.
Component ablations (Transition-only, Hessian-only, KL-only, no-gating, uniform-gating) are the right ablations to isolate each design choice.

Scalability is at least addressed: low-rank (rank-64) blockwise Hessian with windowing and 6-layer sampling for the 70B model, with hyperparameters (beta, gamma, rank, window, batch size, hardware) stated in the main text.
Limitations (runtime, memory, long-text inefficiency) are explicitly acknowledged in the conclusion.

key_concerns.issue: Internal inconsistency in the headline metric: DSA is defined as a difference of normalized attribution masses (total mass sums to 1), which bounds it to [-1, 1], yet Table 1 reports DSA values of 2.10-5.10 (HETA 4.80/5.10). Either the definition or the table is wrong, and the main quantitative claim ('DSA >= 4.2 across all models') is uninterpretable as written. Additionally, the formal definition is circular: S_SciQ and S_NarrQA are defined as 'model-selected important token indices', so the metric appears to be computed over sets selected by the method being evaluated.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Redefine DSA precisely over fixed, annotation-derived token sets (not model-selected ones), state its range, reconcile the reported magnitudes, and re-report all of Table 1 with the corrected definition.

key_concerns.issue: Evaluation circularity: HETA's third component is literally the KL divergence of the target distribution under token masking, and the primary faithfulness metrics (Soft-NC/Soft-NS) also measure output-distribution shift under attribution-guided input perturbation. A method that directly computes per-token masking effects will be near-optimally aligned with masking-based metrics, which plausibly explains the otherwise implausible 3-7x Soft-NC gaps over every baseline. This confound is never discussed, and no metric decorrelated from masking (e.g., erasure-independent sufficiency, downstream counterfactual tasks, or human/ground-truth-rationale evaluation on established datasets) is used as the primary evidence.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one primary evaluation axis that does not reward masking-perturbation agreement (e.g., ground-truth rationale benchmarks such as ERASER-style tasks, or counterfactual task-performance tests), and explicitly analyze the metric-method correlation.

key_concerns.issue: The abstract and contribution list claim 'alignment with human annotations', but the curated dataset's gold labels are the subword intersection of GPT-4o and GPT-5 outputs — no human annotators are involved. This is a material mischaracterization of the evidence and inflates the headline claim.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Relabel as LLM-annotated throughout, add a genuine human annotation subset (even a few hundred instances) to validate the LLM labels, and soften the abstract claim accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: Incomplete evidence for the central comparative claim: the text states HETA exceeds 'the next best method, ReAgent, by over 2x' on GPT-J and Phi-3, but ReAgent rows are absent from the GPT-J and Phi-3 blocks of Table 3 (present only for LLaMA-3.1), and Table 2's DSA row is missing SEA-CoT and ReAgent entries. Qwen2.5-3B, advertised as one of four models, appears only in the appendix. The strongest-baseline comparison is therefore not verifiable from the main results.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report all 10 baselines x all 4 models x all datasets completely, in the main text where space-claimed conclusions depend on them.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical rigor is thin relative to the effect sizes claimed: 3 seeds with 'std < 0.2' / 'std < ±0.06' stated globally rather than per cell, no significance tests, and no investigation of why HETA's Soft-NC (9-11) sits in an entirely different regime from every prior method (~0-4) on the same metric — a gap this large demands a sanity check, not just a mean.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report per-cell mean ± std over seeds, add paired significance tests against the strongest baseline (ReAgent), and include a diagnostic explaining the regime shift (e.g., metric saturation or scale analysis).

key_concerns.issue: Correctness of the Hessian estimator is unclear: Eq. 3 uses Rademacher vectors supported on token i's own block, so it probes only the diagonal block H_ii and captures no cross-token second-order interactions — contradicting the stated motivation of modeling 'second-order interactions between inputs'. As written it is also not a standard unbiased Hutchinson estimator of any named quantity (trace/diagonal), and the number of samples m, runtime, and memory promised ('we report m, runtime, and memory') never appear in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify what quantity Eq. 3 estimates and its bias/variance; if cross-token interaction is claimed, use cross-block probes; report m, wall-clock, and memory per model in the main results.

key_concerns.issue: The KL masking scheme is unspecified ('for a chosen scheme') — mask token, replace with [MASK]/UNK, or ablate embedding? — and beta=gamma=0.5 is asserted without a sensitivity sweep; baseline tuning budgets (especially for the expensive ContextCite) are not described, so fairness of comparison cannot be assessed.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Specify the masking operator, add a beta/gamma sensitivity analysis, and state baseline hyperparameter protocols and compute budgets.

key_concerns.issue: The curated dataset's construction (topically disjoint NarrativeQA distractor + SciQ evidence) makes the 'correct' attribution nearly trivially separable by topic, so high DSA may reflect topic detection rather than causal attribution; the causal-gating component is itself built on attention rollout, which the paper's own motivation section argues is not a faithful causal signal — this tension is unresolved.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add harder curated variants with topically matched distractors, and discuss/empirically test whether the rollout gate inherits the non-causality criticized in attention-based methods.

questions_for_authors: How can DSA exceed 1.0 given its definition as a difference of simplex-normalized masses? Please provide the exact implemented formula and reconcile it with Table 1.

Soft-NC/Soft-NS measure distribution shift under attribution-guided perturbation; HETA's KL term computes distribution shift under masking. Why is this not a circular evaluation, and how do you explain HETA's Soft-NC being 3-7x higher than every published baseline on the identical metric?
Where are the ReAgent rows for GPT-J and Phi-3 in Table 3, given ReAgent is identified as the strongest baseline and the 'over 2x' claim rests on it?
The gold labels come from GPT-4o/GPT-5 intersection. On what basis do you call this 'alignment with human annotations', and what is human agreement with the LLM labels on a validation subset?
With Rademacher probes supported on token i's own block, what cross-token second-order information does Eq. 3 retain, and what are m, runtime, and peak memory per model?
How were baseline hyperparameters and compute budgets (particularly ContextCite's ablation budget) set to ensure a fair comparison?
calibration_check: Claims exceed the evidence: 'alignment with human annotations' rests on LLM-generated labels, 'establishing a new standard' rests on a metric with an internal inconsistency and a masking-based evaluation that favors the method's own masking component, though the limitations section on compute cost is commendably honest.

significance.justification: Faithful attribution for decoder-only LLMs is a real and active problem, and a validated benchmark plus a strong method would be used; impact is capped because the core evidence is currently unreliable.

novelty.justification: The target-conditioned integration of rollout gating, HVP curvature, and KL-masking is a reasonably fresh combination, but each ingredient (attention rollout, Hessian/Integrated-Hessians sensitivity, masking-based KL attribution) is established prior work.

rigor.justification: The DSA definition contradicts its reported values and is circular as written, the Hessian estimator does not capture the cross-token interactions the paper motivates, and the main evaluation is confounded with the method's own masking term.

statistical_soundness.justification: Only 3 seeds, global rather than per-cell std, no significance tests, and implausibly large effect sizes reported without any sanity or regime analysis.

calibration_honesty.justification: LLM-generated labels are presented as 'human annotations', 'new standard' language overclaims, and the metric-method circularity is undisclosed; the honest compute-limitations section partially offsets this.

clarity.justification: Prose motivation and method overview are readable and well organized, but the DSA formal definition is garbled/circular and several key quantities (m, masking scheme) are left vague.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (abstract, intro, motivation, background, method, experiments, ablations, related work, limitations/conclusion) is followed at plausible length.

reproducibility.justification: Hardware, weights, rank, windowing, batch sizes, and grid are specified, but the Hutchinson sample count, masking operator, baseline tuning protocols, and runtime/memory numbers are missing from the main text.

related_work.justification: Coverage of attribution, attention-critique, and recent generative-attribution methods is broad and the criticisms of ContextCite/TDD/PML/ReAgent are specific, though the positioning conveniently omits discussion of perturbation-metric circularity known in this literature.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe genuinely informative items (pipeline overview, component ablations, robustness panels, qualitative attributions), but two of four figures lean on qualitative examples and the tables they accompany contain missing rows.

breadth_generality.justification: Four models, three benchmarks, a curated probe, and nine baselines is good breadth in design, but the strongest baseline is missing from two of three main-table model blocks, Qwen results are appendix-only, and all faithfulness evidence shares one perturbation-based metric family.

overall_recommendation.justification: A promising, well-scoped contribution whose headline evidence is currently undermined by a metric inconsistency, evaluation circularity, and incomplete baseline reporting — fixable, but requiring substantial new analysis and re-reporting (borderline reject).
